To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the crystal and molecular structure was determined from single crystal X-ray data and it is the first structure of d(Cp G) in a left handed Z-Dna form.
the ammonium salt form of d(CpGs) crystallizes as a left handed Z-DNAs.
the structure of the ammoniun salt of d(Cp G) has a left handed Z-DN A helix and the two molecules in the asymmetric unite form a mini left handed helix.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the crystal and molecular structure analysis of the ammonium salts of dinucleotides.
the study of the structural and conformational features of oligonucleotide sequences in the solid state.
the structural characterization of the d(CpG)-NH+4 complex.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the crystal structure of d(CpGs) is the most important and significant contribution to the understanding of the structure of the Z-DNA form of the dinucleotide.
the Z-form of d(CpGs) is a stable structure and that the d(CpG)n sequences have the potential to adopt the Z-form of DNA.

the Z-DNA structure is stabilized in d(CpG)(NH+4) by the interaction of the major groove NH+ ions with N7 atoms of the guanines through a water molecule and the minor groove NH+ ions interact directly with phosphate oxygen atoms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
d(CpG)-NH+4 is an example for a left handed Z-DNAs which can form in the absence of a sequence context.
d(CpG)n sequences are capable of adopting both right and left handed Z-DNAs depending on the length of the sequence.
the d(CpG)-NH+4 salt is a Z-DNA dimer with two NH+4 ions in the crystal lattice, one in the major groove and the other in the minor groove.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the d(CpG)-d(ApT) sequences have the propensity to adopt the left hand Z-DNA structure.
the left-handed Z-DNA conformation is stabilized by the presence of ammonium ions.
the d(CpG)-NH+4 complex represents a model for the recognition of the Z-DNA conformation by a protein.
